knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=A matrix or data.frame containing the beta values (or other real numbers) with genes/probes as row names and samples as column names ;; samples=A data.frame containing sample-to-batch assignments where the first column must be named "sample_id" and the second column "batch_id" ;; adjusted=Logical value in calcBatchEffects indicating whether p-values should be adjusted for multiple testing (default is TRUE) ;; method=The p-value adjustment method in calcBatchEffects (default is "fdr", supports all methods in p.adjust.methods) ;; rowBlockSize=The row size of blocks for dividing the matrix during imputation in imputeMissingData (default is 60; set to 0 to run on the whole matrix without division) ;; colBlockSize=The column size of blocks for dividing the matrix during imputation in imputeMissingData (default is 60; set to 0 to run on the whole matrix without division) ;; epochs=The number of iterations for the gradient descent in imputeMissingData (default is 50) ;; BPPARAM=An optional BiocParallelParam class instance to enable parallelization in calcBatchEffects, imputeMissingData, and correctBatchEffect
- alternatives: None mentioned for batch correction, but the core imputation method is based on Latent Factor Models and stochastic gradient descent techniques.
- when_to_use: Use when you have DNA methylation microarray data (or other high-throughput molecular data represented as a numeric matrix) with known batch assignments, and you need to identify, quantify, and correct batch effects without losing biological variation.
- pitfalls: Imputation can sometimes predict values outside the valid boundaries of beta values (i.e., < 0 or > 1). Users must run replaceOutsideValues to reset these values to 0 or 1. The samples data.frame must strictly have "sample_id" as the first column name and "batch_id" as the second column name.

workflows.name: step_by_step_batch_correction
workflows.intent: Detect, score, and correct batch effects in DNA methylation data using a step-by-step manual workflow.
input: beta_values.csv (Matrix of DNA methylation beta values with genes/probes as rows and samples as columns)
sample_metadata.csv (Data frame with sample_id and batch_id columns mapping samples to their respective batches)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate batch effects (median differences and p-values) using calcBatchEffects ;; 2. Summarize batch-affected gene-sample combinations using calcSummary ;; 3. Calculate batch severity scores using calcScore ;; 4. Set batch-affected values to NA using clearBEgenes ;; 5. Impute the missing values using block-based stochastic gradient descent with imputeMissingData ;; 6. Correct out-of-bounds predicted values using replaceOutsideValues ;; 7. Visualize the distributions before and after correction using makeBoxplot
workflows.code:
batchEffect <- calcBatchEffects(
  data = ex.data, samples = ex.samples,
  adjusted = TRUE, method = "fdr"
)
mdifs <- batchEffect$med
pvals <- batchEffect$pval
summary <- calcSummary(medians = mdifs, pvalues = pvals)
score <- calcScore(ex.data, ex.samples, summary, dir = getwd())
cleared.data <- clearBEgenes(ex.data, ex.samples, summary)
library(ids)
corrected.data <- imputeMissingData(cleared.data,
  rowBlockSize = 60,
  colBlockSize = 60, epochs = 50,
  outputFormat = "", dir = getwd()
)
corrected.data.valid<-replaceOutsideValues(corrected.data)
makeBoxplot(ex.data, ex.samples, score,
  bySamples = TRUE,
  col = "standard", main = "Example data", xlab = "Batch",
  ylab = "Beta value", scoreCol = TRUE)
makeBoxplot(corrected.data, ex.samples, score,
  bySamples = TRUE,
  col = "standard", main = "Corrected example data",
  xlab = "Batch", ylab = "Beta value", scoreCol = FALSE)

workflows.name: one_step_batch_correction
workflows.intent: Perform automated batch effect detection, clearing, and imputation in a single function call.
input: beta_values.csv (Matrix of DNA methylation beta values with genes/probes as rows and samples as columns)
sample_metadata.csv (Data frame with sample_id and batch_id columns mapping samples to their respective batches)
workflows.stages: 1. Run the overall batch correction wrapper function correctBatchEffect
